Sasha: quick idea — we should start cohorting telemetry by low-bit execution path so ops + model teams can see per-path quality drift (fp8 / int8 / 4bit). Currently everything aggregates under 'lowbit' which hides headwise failures.
Amanda: +1. what metrics do you want in the cohort?
Sasha: minimal set: per-request model, quant_profile, precision_lane, token_count, avg_per_token_confidence, degradation_score, char/word-level perplexity (where feasible). Also include 'sampling_bucket' (shadow/production) and an ops tag for rollout id.
Ryan: agree but watch cost. Collecting per-token probs at full fidelity will blow logs. maybe sample 1% of tokens or only for requests flagged by a heuristic (e.g., low conf or long tail prompts).
Maria: for drift detection we don't need every token. repo-level idea: emit summary stats per-request (avg_conf, low_conf_token_count, tail_entropy) and a small histogram for tail severity. if we sample full token traces only for anomalies we keep cost sane.
Sasha: exactly — proposal: two-tier telemetry. 1) lightweight per-request summary always. 2) full-token dump only when degradation_score > 0.6 or for canaries.
Amanda: how do we compute degradation_score in runtime? cheap proxy first: relative drop vs. baseline perplexity + drop in avg_per_token_conf. we can evolve it.
Sasha: runtime placement discussion: do we compute the score in runtime (C++ serving) or post-process in analytics? Pros: runtime can short-circuit and trigger full-token dump. Cons: more risk and release complexity.
Ryan: I'm +post-process for initial rollout to avoid touching runtime. we can add a tiny lib hook that emits per-request summaries (no logic), then analytics computes degradation and flags. once heuristics stabilise we can add runtime gating.
Amanda: ops handoff: we need clear cohort naming and retention. Proposed labels: `quant_profile` (string), `precision_lane` (enum: fp8,int8,4bit,fp16), `cohort` (customer, rollout, canary, shadow). Retention: per-request summary 90 days, full-token dumps 7 days unless retained for triage.
Maria: privacy check — full-token dumps may include PII. we should redact user content or run a PII filter before storing. also encrypt-at-rest and KMS access for full dumps only.
Sasha: good call. add a flag `pii_filtered=true/false` to the metadata and block retention >7 days unless approved by security.
quant-bot: deploy-bot report: Canaries running on `quant-experiment-42` are at 99.98% latency SLO, no errors.
Ryan: one more infra ask: make sure the per-request summary uses protobuf v2 so we can extend fields without breaking ingestion. simple schema: 
```
// summary proto
string request_id
string model
string quant_profile
string precision_lane
int32 token_count
float avg_per_token_conf
float degradation_score
map<string,float> extra_metrics
```
Amanda: sounds good. also add `rollout_id` and `sample_bucket` to proto.
Sasha: ops -> dashboards: create a cohort view (precision_lane x quant_profile) with trend lines for degradation_score, avg_conf, and cost-per-token. include ability to filter by rollout_id.
Maria: alerting: create anomaly detection on cohort-level degradation_score increase > 3 std for 24h or absolute > 0.5 sustained 1h. paging to eng-oncall + model-owner.
Sasha: finalize plan: phase 1 (no runtime changes) implement per-request summary proto + analytics pipeline + dashboards + alerts. phase 2 add runtime gating for full-token dumps and optional on-hotpath short-circuiting.
Amanda: I'll file a short RFC + implementation plan with infra cost estimate. tagging @ryan for ingestion proto and @maria for security review.
Ryan: I'll sketch the proto and a Kinesis -> clickhouse ingestion POC.
Maria: security will review PII filters and retention controls.
Sasha: thanks. can we sync tomorrow 10am? quick 25m to assign owners. :+1:
Amanda: SG.
quant-bot: note created: https://rwood.local/r/telemetry-lowbit-cohorting (placeholder)
